topic: Right of way by road class at entry
idea: Section 48: national, regional and district highways are for high-speed vehicles; when a vehicle enters from a regional highway onto a district highway (or national onto regional) the vehicle on the higher-class road has priority; when entering from one highway to another, vehicles on the highway with higher traffic have priority. A driver entering the main road must stop first (s11(2)(c) offence).
does: Gives unsignalised junctions a priority rule from road class (road type label) or higher flow so the minor road yields and must stop, instead of treating the label as cosmetic
inputs: road type label per road, flows per approach
outputs: priority/yield assignment per junction approach, flagged by analyse_network when equal class
existing: partial: not_built lists 'road types changing behaviour (label stored only)'
notes: Bangladesh law; ACMS can encode it as a selectable rule set (UK/BD) tied to the existing driving-side switch. Rule for flow-based priority needs a flow estimate (demand matrix gives it).

idea: Driver licence has 12 demerit points; offences that deduct them include red-light violation, overtaking near a pedestrian crossing or where prohibited, entering the main road without stopping, speeding over the posted limit, intentionally blocking the road, driving the wrong way on a one-way road, reckless driving/overload, drunk driving. Penalty schedule: speed s44 -> 1 point; overweight s43 -> 2 points; signals s42 -> 1 point.
does: Counts per run the events the Act treats as offences that the sim can detect (speed above limit, red-light entry at junction, stopping outside bus bay, wrong-way) and converts them to demerit points per driver type
inputs: vehicle trace: speed vs limit, signal state at stop line, stopping position
outputs: offence counts by type and road, demerit points
cite: Road Transport Act 2018 s11, s42-s44, s85-s87
notes: Useful as a compliance KPI when testing enforcement or DEVL; drivers in ACMS obey rules by construction except speed factor, so only speeding is naturally measurable.

idea: Government may set time-bound restrictions or peak/off-peak hours for movement of motor vehicles, determine the number of vehicles on a particular road at a specified time, make a lane-based layout of roads in urban areas, and designate bus stops, zebra crossings and overpasses.
does: Scenario test of time-of-day bans (e.g. trucks off a road in peak hours) or vehicle-count caps on a road, rerouting banned types and reporting delay and diversion
inputs: road, vehicle types, time window, cap
notes: Legal basis only; the simulation needs per-road, per-time vehicle class permissions (not built).

idea: Express carriage definition: no stop to pick up passengers at any stoppage less than 32 km from the previous stoppage unless the committee specifies; vehicles may stop only at designated places and times for pickup/drop-off; no boarding or alighting while moving.
does: Lets a bus line be limited-stop with a minimum stop spacing and calls only at listed stops, while stage services call at all stops
inputs: bus line, stop list, minimum spacing
existing: partial: not_built lists 'bus lines calling at some stops only'
cite: Road Transport Act 2018 s2(3), s47(2), s49(1)(g)
notes: 32 km is an intercity figure; urban limited-stop spacing would need another source (Hensher Ch 15 mentions express/skip-stop).

idea: No permanent or temporary establishment may be built on highway land or within 10 m on either side of the slope of the highway; authority may remove it. Moving vehicles may not use the footpath adjacent to the road.
does: Adds a 10 m minimum clear distance from road edge to place_institution/deploy_institutions and flags buildings or stops within it in analyse_network
inputs: institution positions, road geometry and width
notes: Simple geometry; Bangladesh-specific number, make it a parameter.

idea: Ambulances, fire vehicles and rescue vehicles are exempt from route permits (s30(1)(d)) and may use approved sound horns above the normal limit (s45(5)); the Government may determine the fastest time for saving the life of an accident victim (s124(1)(p)); driver involved in an accident must notify police, fire service and hospital immediately.
does: Uses a target 'golden hour' style response time as the pass/fail KPI for emergency vehicle runs (schedule_emergency), reporting arrival time vs the standard
inputs: emergency vehicle trip times in a run
cite: Road Transport Act 2018 s30, s45(5), s124(1)(p)
notes: The Act gives no number for the fastest time and no rule that other traffic must yield; so only the exemption concept is usable. Do not invent a figure.
